This guide explains how to add tests to the Apex test suite. Tests should be added for all new features. Pull Requests must include appropriate tests before they will be merged.

Test Infrastructure Overview

The Apex test suite is built in C and uses a simple, custom test framework. The main components are:

  • tests/test_runner.c - The main test runner that executes all test suites
  • tests/test_helpers.h and tests/test_helpers.c - Shared helper functions and macros
  • Individual test files - Each test file contains one or more test suites (e.g., test_basic.c, test_metadata.c)

Running Tests

Build and run the test suite: 

# Build with CMake
mkdir -p build && cd build
cmake ..
make apex_test_runner

# Run all tests
./apex_test_runner

# Run a specific test suite
./apex_test_runner metadata

# Run with errors-only output (suppress passing tests)
./apex_test_runner --errors-only
./apex_test_runner -e

# Output badge format (passed/total count)
./apex_test_runner --badge

# List available test suites
./apex_test_runner list

When to Create a New Test Suite

Create a new test suite when:

  • Adding a new feature (e.g., citations, indices, a new extension)
  • The feature has multiple test cases that logically group together
  • The tests would clutter an existing suite

Add tests to an existing suite when:

  • Fixing a bug in existing functionality
  • Adding edge cases to existing features
  • The tests naturally fit with related functionality

Test File Structure

Creating a New Test Suite

  1. Create a new test file in tests/ (e.g., tests/test_myfeature.c)

  2. Add the file to CMakeLists.txt: 

add_executable(apex_test_runner
    tests/test_helpers.c
    tests/test_runner.c
    tests/test_basic.c
    # ... other test files ...
    tests/test_myfeature.c  # Add your new file
)
  1. Add a forward declaration in test_runner.c: 
/* Forward declarations for individual test suites */
void test_basic_markdown(void);
void test_gfm_features(void);
// ... other declarations ...
void test_myfeature(void);  // Add your declaration
  1. Register in the suites array in test_runner.c: 
static test_suite suites[] = {
    { "basic", test_basic_markdown },
    // ... other suites ...
    { "myfeature", test_myfeature },  // Add your suite
};

Basic Test File Template 

/**
 * My Feature Tests
 */

#include "test_helpers.h"
#include "apex/apex.h"
#include <string.h>

void test_myfeature(void) {
    int suite_failures = suite_start();
    print_suite_title("My Feature Tests", false, true);

    apex_options opts = apex_options_default();
    char *html;

    /* Test case 1: Basic functionality */
    html = apex_markdown_to_html("# Test", 6, &opts);
    assert_contains(html, "<h1", "Header tag generated");
    apex_free_string(html);

    /* Test case 2: Another test */
    const char *doc = "Some **markdown** content";
    html = apex_markdown_to_html(doc, strlen(doc), &opts);
    assert_contains(html, "<strong>", "Bold text converted");
    apex_free_string(html);

    bool had_failures = suite_end(suite_failures);
    print_suite_title("My Feature Tests", had_failures, false);
}

Helper Functions Reference

Suite Management

suite_start()

Call at the beginning of each test suite to track failures. 

int suite_failures = suite_start();

suite_end(int suite_start_failures)

Call at the end of each test suite. Returns true if any tests failed. 

bool had_failures = suite_end(suite_failures);

print_suite_title(const char *title, bool suite_had_failures, bool at_start)

Prints the suite title. Call twice: once at the start (at_start = true) and once at the end (at_start = false).

  • In normal mode: prints at start
  • In errors-only mode: prints at end only if there were failures
  • In badge mode: never prints 
// At start of suite
print_suite_title("My Feature Tests", false, true);

// At end of suite
print_suite_title("My Feature Tests", had_failures, false);

Assertion Functions

assert_contains(const char *haystack, const char *needle, const char *test_name)

Assert that haystack contains needle. Returns true if found. 

assert_contains(html, "<h1", "Header tag present");
assert_contains(html, "id=\"my-id\"", "Custom ID applied");

assert_not_contains(const char *haystack, const char *needle, const char *test_name)

Assert that haystack does NOT contain needle. Returns true if not found. 

assert_not_contains(html, "<!--TOC-->", "TOC marker replaced");
assert_not_contains(html, "{:.class}", "IAL syntax removed");

assert_option_bool(bool actual, bool expected, const char *test_name)

Assert that a boolean value matches expected. 

assert_option_bool(opts.enable_wiki_links, true, "Wiki links enabled");
assert_option_bool(opts.pretty, false, "Pretty mode disabled");

assert_option_string(const char *actual, const char *expected, const char *test_name)

Assert that a string value matches expected. 

assert_option_string(opts.document_title, "Test Doc", "Title set correctly");

Manual Test Results

test_result(bool passed, const char *test_name)

Report a test result manually when you need custom logic. 

if (strstr(html, "expected") != NULL || strstr(html, "alternative") != NULL) {
    test_result(true, "Expected output found");
} else {
    test_result(false, "Expected output not found");
}

test_resultf(bool passed, const char *format, ...)

Report a test result with a formatted message. 

test_resultf(result == 0, "Function returned %d (expected 0)", result);

Apex API Functions

Core Conversion

apex_markdown_to_html(const char *markdown, size_t length, apex_options *opts)

Convert Markdown to HTML. Returns a dynamically allocated string that must be freed with apex_free_string(). 

char *html = apex_markdown_to_html("# Hello", 7, &opts);
// ... use html ...
apex_free_string(html);

apex_free_string(char *str)

Free a string returned by Apex functions.

Options

apex_options_default()

Get default options (Unified mode with common features enabled). 

apex_options opts = apex_options_default();

apex_options_for_mode(apex_mode mode)

Get options pre-configured for a specific mode. 

apex_options opts = apex_options_for_mode(APEX_MODE_GFM);
apex_options opts = apex_options_for_mode(APEX_MODE_KRAMDOWN);
apex_options opts = apex_options_for_mode(APEX_MODE_MULTIMARKDOWN);
apex_options opts = apex_options_for_mode(APEX_MODE_PANDOC);

apex_apply_metadata_to_options(apex_metadata_item *metadata, apex_options *opts)

Apply metadata key-value pairs to options. Used for testing metadata-driven configuration. 

apex_metadata_item *metadata = NULL;
apex_metadata_item *item = malloc(sizeof(apex_metadata_item));
item->key = strdup("wikilinks");
item->value = strdup("true");
item->next = metadata;
metadata = item;

apex_apply_metadata_to_options(metadata, &opts);
assert_option_bool(opts.enable_wiki_links, true, "wikilinks metadata applied");

apex_free_metadata(metadata);

Metadata

apex_free_metadata(apex_metadata_item *metadata)

Free a metadata linked list.

apex_load_metadata_from_file(const char *path)

Load metadata from a YAML file. Returns NULL on failure. 

#ifdef TEST_FIXTURES_DIR
char path[512];
snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/metadata.yml", TEST_FIXTURES_DIR);
apex_metadata_item *meta = apex_load_metadata_from_file(path);
if (meta) {
    // ... use metadata ...
    apex_free_metadata(meta);
}
#endif

File Includes

apex_process_includes(const char *source, const char *base_dir, const char **search_paths, int search_path_count)

Process file include directives ({{filename}}, <<filename>>, etc.). Returns a new string with includes expanded. 

char *processed = apex_process_includes(source, "tests/fixtures", NULL, 0);
char *html = apex_markdown_to_html(processed, strlen(processed), &opts);
free(processed);
apex_free_string(html);

Common Options for Testing 

apex_options opts = apex_options_default();

// Output options
opts.standalone = true;           // Generate complete HTML document
opts.pretty = true;               // Pretty-print HTML output
opts.document_title = "Test";     // Set document title

// Feature toggles
opts.enable_wiki_links = true;    // Enable [[wiki links]]
opts.enable_spans = true;         // Enable [text]{.class} spans
opts.enable_indices = true;       // Enable index generation
opts.enable_citations = true;     // Enable citation processing
opts.enable_marked_extensions = true;  // Enable TOC, emoji, etc.
opts.enable_smart_typography = true;   // Enable smart quotes
opts.enable_file_includes = true;      // Enable file includes

// Table options
opts.enable_tables = true;        // Enable table processing
opts.relaxed_tables = true;       // Allow relaxed table syntax

// Header options
opts.generate_header_ids = true;  // Generate IDs for headers
opts.header_anchors = true;       // Add anchor links to headers
opts.id_format = 0;               // 0=GFM, 1=MMD, 2=Kramdown

// Citation options
opts.bibliography_files = (char **)files;  // Set bibliography files
opts.link_citations = true;       // Link citations to bibliography
opts.suppress_bibliography = true; // Don't generate bibliography

// Other
opts.base_directory = "tests";    // Base directory for file resolution
opts.enable_aria = true;          // Add ARIA accessibility attributes

Complete Test Example

Here’s a complete example testing a hypothetical “highlight” feature: 

/**
 * Highlight Extension Tests
 */

#include "test_helpers.h"
#include "apex/apex.h"
#include <string.h>

void test_highlight(void) {
    int suite_failures = suite_start();
    print_suite_title("Highlight Extension Tests", false, true);

    apex_options opts = apex_options_default();
    opts.enable_highlight = true;
    char *html;

    /* Test basic highlight syntax */
    const char *basic = "This is ==highlighted== text.";
    html = apex_markdown_to_html(basic, strlen(basic), &opts);
    assert_contains(html, "<mark>", "Highlight uses mark tag");
    assert_contains(html, "highlighted", "Highlight content preserved");
    assert_contains(html, "</mark>", "Highlight tag closed");
    assert_not_contains(html, "==", "Highlight syntax removed");
    apex_free_string(html);

    /* Test highlight with other inline formatting */
    const char *mixed = "This is ==**bold highlight**== here.";
    html = apex_markdown_to_html(mixed, strlen(mixed), &opts);
    assert_contains(html, "<mark>", "Highlight with nested bold");
    assert_contains(html, "<strong>", "Bold inside highlight");
    apex_free_string(html);

    /* Test multiple highlights */
    const char *multi = "First ==one== and ==two== highlights.";
    html = apex_markdown_to_html(multi, strlen(multi), &opts);
    /* Count occurrences */
    int count = 0;
    const char *p = html;
    while ((p = strstr(p, "<mark>")) != NULL) {
        count++;
        p++;
    }
    test_resultf(count == 2, "Multiple highlights: found %d (expected 2)", count);
    apex_free_string(html);

    /* Test highlight disabled */
    apex_options no_hl = apex_options_default();
    no_hl.enable_highlight = false;
    html = apex_markdown_to_html(basic, strlen(basic), &no_hl);
    assert_not_contains(html, "<mark>", "Highlight disabled produces no mark tags");
    assert_contains(html, "==highlighted==", "Highlight syntax preserved when disabled");
    apex_free_string(html);

    /* Test edge case: empty highlight */
    const char *empty = "This is ==== empty.";
    html = apex_markdown_to_html(empty, strlen(empty), &opts);
    /* Empty highlight should not create mark tag */
    if (strstr(html, "<mark></mark>") == NULL) {
        test_result(true, "Empty highlight handled gracefully");
    } else {
        test_result(false, "Empty highlight creates empty mark tag");
    }
    apex_free_string(html);

    /* Test highlight across lines (should not work) */
    const char *multiline = "This is ==high\nlighted== text.";
    html = apex_markdown_to_html(multiline, strlen(multiline), &opts);
    assert_not_contains(html, "<mark>", "Highlight does not span lines");
    apex_free_string(html);

    bool had_failures = suite_end(suite_failures);
    print_suite_title("Highlight Extension Tests", had_failures, false);
}

Using Test Fixtures

For tests that need external files, use the TEST_FIXTURES_DIR macro: 

#ifdef TEST_FIXTURES_DIR
char fixture_path[512];
snprintf(fixture_path, sizeof(fixture_path), "%s/mytest.md", TEST_FIXTURES_DIR);

FILE *fp = fopen(fixture_path, "rb");
if (fp) {
    // Read and process file
    fclose(fp);
} else {
    test_result(false, "Failed to load test fixture");
}
#endif

Test fixture files should be placed in tests/fixtures/ in an appropriate subdirectory.

Best Practices

  1. Always free allocated memory - Use apex_free_string() for Apex-allocated strings
  2. Test both positive and negative cases - Verify features work AND don’t appear when disabled
  3. Use descriptive test names - The test name appears in output on failure
  4. Test edge cases - Empty input, special characters, boundary conditions
  5. Test mode-specific behavior - If a feature behaves differently in different modes, test each mode
  6. Keep tests focused - Each test should verify one specific behavior
  7. Use strlen() for variable-length input - Pass correct length to apex_markdown_to_html() 
// For string literals, you can count manually or use strlen
html = apex_markdown_to_html("# Test", 6, &opts);

// For variable content, always use strlen
const char *doc = some_variable_content;
html = apex_markdown_to_html(doc, strlen(doc), &opts);

Global Variables

The test framework uses these global variables (defined in test_helpers.c):

  • tests_run - Total number of tests executed
  • tests_passed - Number of passing tests
  • tests_failed - Number of failing tests
  • errors_only_output - When non-zero, only print failing tests
  • badge_mode - When non-zero, suppress output except final count
